policy.definition: Parity means user-visible behavior and supported platform coverage match the pinned Magpie desktop baseline, not line-by-line source compatibility.
policy.upstream_change_rule: New Magpie behavior changes are added only by creating a new baseline with a new pinned commit, updated capabilities, and a recorded impact review.

capabilities.title: Provider presets
acceptance: All provider presets listed by the pinned Magpie README can be selected and produce valid defaults.

capabilities.title: Custom compatible endpoints
acceptance: Users can add arbitrary OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible base URLs with per-provider headers.

capabilities.title: Vendor model discovery
acceptance: Provider model lists can be fetched, refreshed, cached, and merged with models.dev metadata.

capabilities.title: Model capability metadata
acceptance: Model names, API protocol, context size, reasoning levels, and price metadata drive the UI and gateway.

capabilities.title: Provider imports
acceptance: CC Switch, Claude Code, Codex, and Alma configurations can be discovered, previewed, imported, and deduplicated.

capabilities.title: Add-to-Magpie links
acceptance: Signed import links open a confirmation sheet and add the described provider without silently trusting the payload.

capabilities.title: Global profiles
acceptance: A profile saves and atomically restores every agent binding, model shortlist, and relevant routing preference.

capabilities.title: Per-key and per-account proxy
acceptance: Each provider key or account can use a named proxy independently of global networking.

capabilities.title: Subscription inventory
acceptance: Installed and signed-in subscription accounts are discovered without exposing credentials.

capabilities.title: Claude subscription adapter
acceptance: Claude subscription models can be signed in, refreshed, routed, and bridged with tool calls.

capabilities.title: Codex and ChatGPT subscription adapter
acceptance: ChatGPT plan accounts can be refreshed, switched, and exposed to other agents through the gateway.

capabilities.title: GitHub Copilot adapter
acceptance: GitHub.com and enterprise Copilot accounts can be added and failed over.

capabilities.title: Gemini Code Assist adapter
acceptance: Google subscription accounts and project selection drive Gemini model access and quota reads.

capabilities.title: Antigravity adapter
acceptance: Antigravity accounts are driven through the supported local CLI with tool bridging.

capabilities.title: Grok subscription adapter
acceptance: Grok plan models and supported video generation are available through the account adapter.

capabilities.title: OpenCode auth plugins
acceptance: OpenCode auth plugins and pi packages can sign in, list models, and serve requests.

capabilities.title: Multi-account failover
acceptance: Quota, 429, authentication, timeout, and outage failures advance to another eligible account without leaking the original failure unless all candidates fail.

capabilities.title: Account warm-up
acceptance: Daily and reset-based warm-ups start supported quota windows at configured times without running while the computer sleeps.

capabilities.title: Account export and import
acceptance: Supported account files can be imported or exported in Magpie and common compatibility formats with explicit credential warnings.

capabilities.title: OpenAI Chat Completions protocol
acceptance: OpenAI Chat requests complete, stream, and invoke tools through the local gateway.

capabilities.title: OpenAI Responses protocol
acceptance: Responses requests support text, streaming, tools, reasoning, cancellation, and usage.

capabilities.title: Anthropic Messages protocol
acceptance: Anthropic requests support content blocks, streaming, tools, thinking, and usage.

capabilities.title: Gemini protocol
acceptance: Gemini generateContent requests support streaming, function calls, safety fields, and usage.

capabilities.title: Streaming translation
acceptance: Every supported inbound protocol can stream from every supported upstream without buffering the full response.

capabilities.title: Tool call translation
acceptance: Tool schemas, calls, argument deltas, results, and errors survive cross-protocol routing.

capabilities.title: Reasoning translation
acceptance: Reasoning levels and reasoning content are translated or deliberately suppressed according to model capabilities.

capabilities.title: Cross-protocol conversion
acceptance: All supported inbound and upstream protocol pairs pass the same behavioral conformance corpus.

capabilities.title: Local gateway endpoint
acceptance: A stable loopback endpoint exposes health, model discovery, protocol routes, and warnings for incompatible clients.

capabilities.title: Gateway request identity
acceptance: Every request has a stable ID propagated through routing, logs, usage, traces, and client errors.

capabilities.title: Gateway middleware
acceptance: Middleware hooks can change requests, inspect stream events, alter responses, time out, and fail open as specified.

capabilities.title: Gateway failure semantics
acceptance: Client disconnect, cancellation, upstream timeout, malformed upstream data, and all-candidates-failed are distinguishable and auditable.

capabilities.title: Routing groups
acceptance: A group combines providers, accounts, models, and nested groups under one model identifier.

capabilities.title: Smart routing
acceptance: Smart mode uses eligible subscriptions that renew soonest while respecting remaining quota and candidate health.

capabilities.title: Ordered failover
acceptance: Order mode uses the first eligible member and advances only after a retryable failure.

capabilities.title: Rotating selection
acceptance: Rotate mode advances deterministically across eligible members while honoring session rules.

capabilities.title: Least-used routing
acceptance: Usage mode selects by the configured token or request window and updates its counters atomically.

capabilities.title: Paced quota routing
acceptance: Pace mode compares remaining weekly quota per hour until reset and avoids exhausting soon-resetting accounts incorrectly.

capabilities.title: Weighted routing
acceptance: Weighted groups distribute eligible requests according to configured member weights and health.

capabilities.title: Nested groups
acceptance: Groups may contain groups without recursive selection loops or hidden duplicate candidates.

capabilities.title: Session stickiness
acceptance: A conversation remains on the selected account while cache value and eligibility remain valid.

capabilities.title: Intent routing
acceptance: A configurable classifier routes new turns to the chosen model class and records the decision trace.

capabilities.title: Model constraints
acceptance: Busy load, context limits, disabled models, budgets, allowed accounts, and free/cheap/fast preferences constrain candidates.

capabilities.title: Live routing trace
acceptance: The UI shows candidate filtering, selected member, failover attempts, and reason for each decision.

capabilities.title: Supported agent catalog
acceptance: Every agent in the pinned agent-catalog.json has a discoverable adapter or a documented compatibility path and automated fixture tests.

capabilities.title: Installed agent discovery
acceptance: Only installed agents are shown, with installation source, version, configuration location, and platform details.

capabilities.title: Transactional config edits
acceptance: Agent edits preserve formatting where supported, use locks and atomic replacement, verify the result, and can roll back.

capabilities.title: Cross-agent model picker
acceptance: Users can search and bind every eligible provider/model from one list while unsupported choices are disabled with reasons.

capabilities.title: Per-agent model shortlist
acceptance: Each agent can expose a curated model list that profiles preserve and restore.

capabilities.title: Agent version and update
acceptance: The app reports installed versions, uses the matching installation method to update, and shows install commands for missing agents.

capabilities.title: Cross-agent library
acceptance: Instructions, MCP servers, skills, and subagents can be written to each supported agent in its native format and removed without deleting user-owned content.

capabilities.title: Restore agent defaults
acceptance: A user can remove Magpie-managed model settings and recover the exact pre-management agent configuration.

capabilities.title: Windows WSL integration
acceptance: Agents in supported WSL distributions are discovered, configured, versioned, and counted for usage.

capabilities.title: Tokens and cost accounting
acceptance: Every request records input, output, cached, reasoning, and total tokens plus estimated cost.

capabilities.title: Cache and reasoning metrics
acceptance: Cache reads, cache writes, reasoning tokens, and call counts are retained per request and aggregate.

capabilities.title: Custom model prices
acceptance: Users can override model prices and currencies without changing historical recorded costs.

capabilities.title: Balances and quota
acceptance: Quota and balance readers cover supported API keys, plans, and subscription accounts and expose unknown states explicitly.

capabilities.title: Quota windows
acceptance: Five-hour, weekly, monthly, and provider-specific windows retain reset times and remaining amounts.

capabilities.title: Quota history
acceptance: Quota readings are retained for the baseline-defined history period and can be queried by provider or account.

capabilities.title: Usage alerts
acceptance: Quota, balance, reset, and task-done alerts are configurable and deduplicated.

capabilities.title: Session usage history
acceptance: Agent sessions list title, cost, model, folder, and timestamps and can reopen the session in its native terminal.

capabilities.title: Context utilization
acceptance: Each request shows context-window use, cache contribution, and major context categories.

capabilities.title: Account and key bills
acceptance: Costs can be grouped by account and upstream key for the selected period.

capabilities.title: OTLP export
acceptance: Configured OTLP endpoints receive trace and usage data with redaction and retry controls.

capabilities.title: Usage CSV export
acceptance: CSV exports include the baseline request fields and honor account and time-window filters.

capabilities.title: Deterministic masking rules
acceptance: Secrets and personal data are detected with configurable built-in and user-defined rules before upstream transmission.

capabilities.title: Local PII model
acceptance: The optional local model detects non-rule-based names, addresses, and passwords without uploading the inspected prompt.

capabilities.title: Stable placeholders
acceptance: The same detected value receives the same opaque placeholder for the applicable scope and cache lifetime.

capabilities.title: Restore placeholders everywhere
acceptance: Placeholders are restored in buffered text, streamed text, reasoning, and tool-call arguments before the agent observes them.

capabilities.title: Mask, warn, and block policies
acceptance: Each rule can mask, warn about, or block a request according to user configuration.

capabilities.title: Masking audit
acceptance: The audit lists changed requests with redacted vendor payloads, rule matches, and restoration outcomes without storing secret values.

capabilities.title: Fail-closed masking
acceptance: When enabled masking cannot run, the request is blocked with a clear 503 response rather than sent unmasked.

capabilities.title: Web search for any model
acceptance: Models without native search receive the same web_search tool through the gateway and MCP.

capabilities.title: Web fetch
acceptance: Agents can fetch a URL through a filtered, size-limited, redacted web_fetch tool.

capabilities.title: Search key rotation
acceptance: Search APIs support multiple keys, order or rotation selection, refusal cooldown, and quota visibility.

capabilities.title: MCP servers
acceptance: stdio and HTTP MCP servers can connect, list tools, authenticate, and be exposed to OpenTalos and gateway clients.

capabilities.title: Browser MCP and extension
acceptance: A browser extension exposes controlled browser tools through MCP with explicit user-visible permissions.

capabilities.title: Image generation MCP
acceptance: Any configured agent can invoke image generation through an MCP tool and receive persisted media references.

capabilities.title: Video generation MCP
acceptance: Supported Grok and MiniMax video paths are exposed through the generation MCP server with progress and cancellation.

capabilities.title: Long-term memory
acceptance: Memory extraction, embedding, consolidation, retrieval, and deletion remain compatible with existing OpenTalos memory settings.

capabilities.title: Plugin discovery
acceptance: Built-in and community plugins can be searched, installed, updated, disabled, and removed with integrity checks.

capabilities.title: Provider plugins
acceptance: A Bun plugin can sign in, list models, and serve requests through the unified provider interface.

capabilities.title: Plugin gateway middleware
acceptance: Plugin hooks can implement the baseline request, event, and response middleware contract with timeout isolation.

capabilities.title: Plugin UI slots
acceptance: Plugin pages, settings, and registered slots render without gaining access outside their declared capabilities.

capabilities.title: Menu bar application
acceptance: The desktop app runs from the macOS menu bar and the Windows/Linux tray without requiring the main window.

capabilities.title: Animated tray icon
acceptance: Opening the quick panel plays the animated tray sequence and tolerates repeated clicks.

capabilities.title: Main application window
acceptance: The main window preserves OpenTalos navigation and supports platform-correct resize, minimize, maximize, close, and restore.

capabilities.title: Quick panel
acceptance: A compact panel opens under the tray icon, fits content, follows text size, and closes on outside click where supported.

capabilities.title: Multiple app windows
acceptance: Main, quick panel, remote, and plugin-created windows have isolated lifecycle and deterministic shutdown.

capabilities.title: Keep window on top
acceptance: The main and panel windows can be pinned according to platform capability with visible state.

capabilities.title: Global shortcuts
acceptance: The quick panel and settings shortcuts register, conflict-check, and unregister cleanly.

capabilities.title: Application themes
acceptance: Light, dark, system, text size, and supported Linux theme integrations match the baseline and remain readable.

capabilities.title: Single instance
acceptance: A second launch hands URLs and commands to the existing process and exits without duplicating tray or gateway services.

capabilities.title: Application deep links
acceptance: OpenTalos and Magpie import URL schemes register and open the confirmed UI flow on supported platforms.

capabilities.title: Open at login
acceptance: Autostart can be enabled, disabled, inspected, and repaired across macOS, Windows, and Linux.

capabilities.title: Keep awake
acceptance: The app can prevent sleep while active and restores the platform power state on exit.

capabilities.title: Native notifications
acceptance: Alerts use native notifications with permission handling, click routing, and deduplication.

capabilities.title: Accessibility and keyboard navigation
acceptance: Keyboard focus, screen-reader labels, zoom, reduced motion, and high-contrast behavior pass desktop UI checks.

capabilities.title: Browser web mode
acceptance: The OpenTalos React UI remains usable in a browser with explicit desktop-only features disabled.

capabilities.title: Terminal UI
acceptance: A terminal interface exposes the baseline agent, provider, routing, usage, groups, sessions, and library pages.

capabilities.title: Command line interface
acceptance: The pinned baseline CLI commands and machine-readable outputs are available with compatible exit codes.

capabilities.title: Linux desktop integration
acceptance: Hyprland, niri, KWin, Omarchy, and tray fallback behavior match the supported Linux baseline.

capabilities.title: Local network sharing
acceptance: Gateway sharing can be enabled on selected interfaces with explicit network exposure warnings.

capabilities.title: Named gateway keys
acceptance: Named client keys can be created, rotated, moved, revoked, and audited.

capabilities.title: Gateway key budgets
acceptance: Daily, weekly, monthly, token, cost, cache, and concurrency limits are enforced atomically.

capabilities.title: Gateway key access control
acceptance: Keys can be limited to models, accounts, account groups, MCP servers, read-only operations, and admin scopes.

capabilities.title: TLS and mTLS
acceptance: Custom TLS, Magpie-issued certificates, client certificates, revocation, and permission errors are supported.

capabilities.title: Remote Magpie
acceptance: A local client can use another Magpie's providers and routes while managing its own agent configuration.

capabilities.title: Administrative API
acceptance: Authorized keys can manage providers, accounts, groups, and keys through documented endpoints with local/admin scopes.

capabilities.title: OIDC-issued short-lived keys
acceptance: Approved OIDC claims can exchange a trusted identity token for a constrained short-lived gateway key.

capabilities.title: Docker and server mode
acceptance: The gateway and web UI run headlessly in a supported image with health checks, persistent data, and TLS-compatible configuration.

capabilities.title: Issued short-lived keys
acceptance: An issuer key can create constrained keys with explicit TTL, models, accounts, limits, and audit records.

capabilities.title: Backup and restore
acceptance: Selective backup and restore cover providers, keys, settings, profiles, agents, library, sign-ins, and encrypted archives.

capabilities.title: WebDAV sync
acceptance: Encrypted or configurable WebDAV sync detects conflicts and never overwrites newer local state silently.

capabilities.title: S3-compatible sync
acceptance: S3-compatible storage can hold versioned, encrypted backups with retry and conflict handling.

capabilities.title: Encrypted GitHub sync
acceptance: An authorized GitHub repository can store encrypted backups without exposing credentials or plaintext.

capabilities.title: Background service mode
acceptance: Gateway-only service mode installs, starts, stops, survives reboot, and reports status through native service managers.

capabilities.title: Safe uninstall
acceptance: Uninstall restores every managed agent before removing Magpie files, with keep-data and purge choices.

capabilities.title: Logs and diagnostics
acceptance: Users can locate and tail logs and export redacted heap, CPU, goroutine-equivalent, process, and version diagnostics.

capabilities.title: Runtime status and health
acceptance: Health and status report the serving process, role, version, listen address, gateway state, and desktop supervisor state.

capabilities.title: Proxy configuration
acceptance: Global, provider, plugin-download, and update proxies support system settings, explicit URLs, validation, and connectivity tests.

capabilities.title: Network safety
acceptance: Loopback, LAN, TLS, SSRF, DNS rebinding, proxy, and upstream redirect behavior pass security tests.

capabilities.title: Crash recovery
acceptance: Desktop supervisor restarts failed sidecars, preserves data, reports crash loops, and never leaves orphan child processes.

capabilities.title: Desktop packaging
acceptance: Reproducible one-folder builds launch without external Python or Node installations on all supported platforms.

capabilities.title: macOS signing and notarization
acceptance: macOS artifacts are signed, hardened-runtime compatible, notarized, stapled, and verified on clean machines.

capabilities.title: Windows signing and installer
acceptance: Windows artifacts are Authenticode-signed, install per-user safely, preserve data on upgrade, and pass SmartScreen checks.

capabilities.title: Linux packages
acceptance: Supported distributions can install and remove AppImage, deb, or rpm artifacts without dependency conflicts.

capabilities.title: Automatic updates
acceptance: Updates verify signatures and manifests, use atomic handoff, preserve data, recover from failure, and never update during active unsafe operations.

capabilities.title: Build attestations
acceptance: Release artifacts have verifiable provenance and installers can document how users verify them.

capabilities.title: License and third-party notices
acceptance: Every package includes MIT attribution and third-party notices for Python, Qt, Node, Bun, models, fonts, and copied Magpie code.

capabilities.title: Data migration and downgrade safety
acceptance: Every release migrates OpenTalos data transactionally, creates a backup, and blocks downgrade when data would be lost.
